newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to cover domestic debt with new issues.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to cover domestic debt with new issues.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance ministry plans to meet most of pending maturity and interest payments on treasury paper by new issues of government securities, a Finance Ministry official said.
"The larger part of pending payments on government debt will be covered through regular treasury paper issues," the Head of State Treasury and Debt department Plamen Oresharski told Reuters.
"Treasury paper liquidity has declined now because of the restrictive monetary policy of the central bank, but commercial banks have almost no other investment alternatives," Plamen Oresharski said.
The Bulgarian National Bank strictly limits the foreign exchange positions of financial institutions, which deters them from speculative foreign currency purchases.
Bulgaria's government domestic debt rose to 599.8 billion levs in August from 582.5 billion levs at the end of July and 345.4 billion levs at the end of 1995, Finance Ministry figures show.
"The monthly rise was due to net sales of government paper and the lev's fall against the dollar last month," Oresharski said.
The lev's decline in August increased the price in levs of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds and bonds issued under the deposit guarantee bill.
The lev fell from 187 against the dollar at the beginning of August to 208 at the end of the month.

Financial institutions hold around $964 million worth of T-bonds, issued by the government in 1994 to cover non-performing debts of state companies to commercial banks accumulated by 1991, figures show.
This year the Finance Ministry issued $61 billion worth of floater coupon T-bonds to guarantee hard currency deposits in banks which the central bank seeks to close down.
The ministry sold treasury paper worth of some 22 billion levs last month while maturity payments alone totalled around 17 billion levs.

For the first eight months of this year financial institutions bought 191.693 billion levs worth of treasury issues and companies and individuals invested 11.068 billion levs in government paper, figures showed.

Budget revenue from treasury paper sales from January through August totalled 189.266 billion levs, while interest and principal payments for the same period amounted to 175.691 billion levs, figures showed.
Treasury issues with a total par of 241.089 billion levs were in circulation at the end of August.

Government's debt to the Bulgarian National Bank, the State Savings Bank and the State Insurance Institute edged down to 43.690 billion levs at the end of August from 43.979 billion a month earlier, figures showed. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
